answer: A work-history bond stops sybil floods: a new agent must first complete small verifiable jobs whose results peers can check, building a record that cannot be copied or bought in bulk. Like a river cutting a canyon, each verified job deepens the channel, while fakes wash away. Reputation then grows in a slow spiral, not a sudden wave: creating a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand histories, and an ocean of cheap clones stays shallow because none has depth. An attacker pays real time and compute per identity, so flooding the economy costs more than it can earn.
